title: Segmented Access Controller: token-bucket prioritization and graceful variant downgrade
creator: Marco Delgado
description: Implement a segmented access controller that enforces quota-aware prioritization across customer segments (free / paid / enterprise) using a deterministic token-bucket admission policy. When capacity or per-tenant credits are constrained, the controller should (a) admit requests according to segment-weighted buckets, (b) probabilistically spill low-priority requests to lower-cost model variants or regional spillover targets, and (c) surface deterministic signals to Console for billing and SLO reconciliation. The feature must preserve tail-latency SLOs for enterprise lanes while enabling graceful degradation for free tier traffic via model-variant downgrades and temporary local caching. This ticket covers design, core algorithm, API hooks, and an incremental rollout to production clusters.
acceptance_criteria: Admission controller enforces per-segment token buckets and respects plan weights for admission decisions in 95% of decision windows.
When global capacity exceeds configured threshold, free-tier requests are routed to quantized model variant or regional spill target with documented fallback order.
Telemetry events emitted for every admission/deny/spill with fields: user_tier, tenant_id_hash, decision, chosen_variant, region, remaining_tokens.
Console shows a breakdown of rejected vs spilled requests by tier and supports a toggle to simulate policy for 24h before enforcement.
No regression in enterprise 99th percentile latency (>1ms delta) on canary cluster during rollout.
Automated integration tests validate token-bucket exhaustion scenarios, simultaneous multi-tenant bursts, and variant downgrade paths.
Runbook updated with steps to disable policy, adjust weights, and emergency rollback instructions.
technical_notes: Primary admission primitive: deterministic token-bucket per (tenant, tier) computed from plan quotas + ephemeral burst capacity shared pool.
Admission scoring: score = base_weight(tier) * priority_boost(enterprise_degrade_flag) - cost_penalty(chosen_variant). Admission if score > threshold and token available.

Spill strategy: ordered fallback list: same-region compatible quantized variant -> cross-region same-tier -> best-effort cached response -> deny. Use probabilistic selection when multiple spill targets available to avoid hot-spots.
Model variants are treated as labeled capabilities; admission controller must be model-agnostic and reference variant compatibility matrix from model catalog service.
Telemetry schema: emit compact JSON line per decision to kafka topic 'admissions.v1' and enrich with route/model metadata downstream.
Locality: prefer region affinity for enterprise; allow cross-region spill only when latency penalty < configured SLO delta.

Concurrency model: admission decisions are made at gateway side with eventual consistency for token counts using a leaky counter + optimistic decrement. Fallback to central arbiter for contested bursts (configurable).
Safety nets: circuit breaker on per-tenant denial rate; automatic weight increase if enterprise SLOs approach threshold.
rollout_plan: 1) Unit + integration tests covering token-bucket and spill paths (branch: feat/segmented-access-controller).
2) Internal canary: enable policy in 'dry-run' mode (telemetry only) for 48h in staging and one production region with low traffic (tag: canary-us-west-2).
3) Partial enforcement: enforce for 5% of free-tier traffic with monitoring dashboards and automatic rollback triggers tied to latency and error budgets.
4) Progressive increase: 5% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% over 5 days with manual checkpoints and QA sign-off between steps.
5) Enable simulation toggle in Console for account owners to preview how many of their requests would be spilled/denied in the last 24h.
6) Full rollout once telemetry shows stable metrics and no enterprise regressions.
metrics: Enterprise p99 latency: target no more than +1ms regression vs baseline.
Free-tier spill rate: monitored and adjustable; default target <30% under normal load.
Admission decision accuracy: token-bucket enforcement matches expected token counts >= 99% in synthetic load tests.
Telemetry event volume: ensure sampling when traffic > 10k rps to avoid telemetry overload.
Operational alerts: cross-region spill > 5% sustained for 15 minutes, enterprise p99 increase > 2ms, per-tenant denial rate > 1% for > 10 minutes.
risks: Optimistic local counters can lead to transient over-admission under synchronized bursts; mitigated by central arbiter fallback and short ballot windows.
Spill to cross-region variants may violate data residency constraints for some customers—policy must respect tenant restrictions from profile store.
Telemetry volume growth may increase cost; implement sampling and summarization at gateway.
Incorrect weight tuning could starve paid customers—include automated safety checks and manual override in Console.
